Focal nodular hyperplasia (FNH)
Keyword findings: homogeneously and brightly enhancing mass; central scar; became isodense with liver on portal venous phase; retains contrast more than underlying liver; central scar does not take up or retain gadoxetate
Reasoning: The cluster shows the classic combination of homogeneous arterial hyperenhancement with later near-isodensity and hepatobiliary contrast retention by the mass but not by the central scar.
column9:
Key differentiators: FNH favors homogeneous arterial enhancement, later near-isodensity/isointensity, Eovist retention by the lesion, and lack of gadoxetate retention by the central scar. Core validation also supports a T2-bright scar and late extracellular-contrast scar enhancement. Adenoma can mimic a scar through hemorrhage/necrosis/fibrosis/fat; fibrolamellar HCC favors young noncirrhotic context, large heterogeneous mass, T1/T2-dark fibrotic or calcified scar, and nodal/aggressive features; giant hemangioma favors blood-pool peripheral nodular enhancement and very bright T2 signal. Imaging specificity: Strongly suggestive when the full pattern is present.

Liver Mass With Central or Eccentric Scar

Source Basis: Core Radiology validation report + RadPrimer + STATdx master-source synthesis
Summary
  • Central-scar liver-mass workup should first separate a true scar from necrosis, hemorrhage, fat, fibrosis, or treated tumor.
  • Key image pivots are scar calcification, dynamic enhancement of the mass and scar, hepatobiliary contrast behavior, multiplicity, and associated vascular invasion, biliary obstruction, capsular retraction, or Budd-Chiari morphology.
  • FNH: homogeneous arterial hyperenhancement, later near-isodensity/isointensity, T2-bright scar, late extracellular-contrast scar enhancement, Eovist retention by the lesion, and no gadoxetate retention by the central scar. Core also supports spoke-wheel Doppler and sulfur colloid/HIDA confirmation of functioning components.
  • Hemangioma: peripheral discontinuous nodular blood-pool enhancement with progressive centripetal fill-in, T2 hyperintensity, and classic echogenic avascular ultrasound appearance with possible posterior enhancement.
  • Conventional HCC: arterial enhancement, portal/delayed washout, enhancing capsule, mosaic/necrotic architecture when large, and vascular invasion as a report-critical pivot.
  • Fibrolamellar HCC: young noncirrhotic patient, large heterogeneous mass, fibrotic T1/T2-dark central scar, scar calcification, no true capsule, and possible nodal/aggressive disease.
  • Adenoma: arterial hyperenhancement with possible fat/hemorrhage; chemical-shift signal drop supports intralesional fat, HIDA/sulfur-colloid nonuptake helps separate it from FNH, and size >5 cm is a management pivot because of hemorrhage risk.
  • Metastases: multiplicity, hypovascular portal-venous conspicuity, central necrosis/fibrosis, mucinous calcification, and variable MRI signal patterns depending on content.
  • Cholangiocarcinoma: delayed/progressive fibrotic enhancement plus capsular retraction, hepatic volume loss, biliary obstruction, or portal venous obstruction.
  • EHE: multiple peripheral/subcapsular target lesions with capsular retraction; source MRI shows T2 hyperintense central necrosis/scar in peripheral confluent masses.
  • Budd-Chiari/large regenerative nodules: multiple hypervascular nodules with central scars or doughnut enhancement; gadobenate retention indicates functional hepatocytes with deficient biliary ducts.

Giant cavernous hemangioma
Keyword findings: peripheral nodular enhancement; central scar; small focus of calcification; did not fill in on delayed imaging; very bright; progressive nodular enhancement
Reasoning: The peripheral nodular blood-pool enhancement with progressive fill-in and very bright T2 signal strongly supports a giant hemangioma, with a central nonenhancing scar/degenerative region.

column5:
Conventional hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
Keyword findings: large, heterogeneous, hypervascular mass; foci of necrosis; mottled or mosaic appearance; absence of calcification; eccentric scar or necrotic area; tumor invasion of portal vein
Reasoning: The large heterogeneous hypervascular mass with necrosis/mosaic architecture is compatible with HCC; portal vein tumor invasion is a major discriminator from many mimics and supports conventional HCC over fibrolamellar HCC in this pattern.
column9:
Key differentiators: Portal or hepatic venous invasion strongly favors HCC. Core also describes arterial enhancement with portal venous washout and enhancing capsule as the classic HCC pattern. Scar calcification is rare in conventional HCC. Imaging specificity: Strongly suggestive.

Hepatic adenoma
Keyword findings: heterogeneous mass; focus of high attenuation; hemorrhage; lower density foci; necrosis and fibrosis; central nonenhancing scar
Reasoning: The apparent central scar pattern is explained by hemorrhage, necrosis, and fibrosis rather than a classic true scar, a major pitfall in adenoma.
column9:
Key differentiators: Adenoma often contains fat, hemorrhage, necrosis, or fibrosis that can mimic a scar. Chemical-shift signal drop supports intracellular fat, and hepatobiliary contrast behavior helps distinguish adenoma from FNH. Imaging specificity: Nonspecific without full characterization.

Hepatic metastases from colon cancer
Keyword findings: multiple lesions; faint central calcification; multiple metastases; central, low-density necrosis or fibrosis; faint calcification
Reasoning: Multiplicity plus central necrosis/fibrosis and faint calcification supports metastases; the source specifically notes calcification can occur in mucinous metastases such as colon cancer.

Mucinous metastases may calcify; multiplicity and a portal-venous hypovascular pattern support metastases. Imaging specificity: Strongly suggestive in the appropriate clinical setting.

Fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma
Keyword findings: heterogeneous, hypervascular mass; large, calcified central scar; similar enhancement of tumor in a cardiophrenic node; central necrotic scar; low density portions of the scar; calcified portions of the scar
Reasoning: The combination of a large heterogeneous hypervascular mass in a young patient with a large calcified central scar and nodal disease is classic for fibrolamellar HCC.
column9:

FNH favors homogeneous arterial enhancement with Eovist retention by the mass; giant hemangioma favors peripheral nodular blood-pool enhancement and very bright T2 signal; conventional HCC is supported by older/background risk context and tumor-in-vein when present. Imaging specificity: Strongly suggestive when the full pattern is present.

Mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
Keyword findings: foci of scar or necrosis; capsular retraction; occlusion of the portal vein; bile duct; progressive enhancement on arterial, portal venous, and delayed phases; fibrotic changes; nonenhancing central scar
Reasoning: Progressive delayed enhancement reflects the fibrotic tumor stroma, while capsular retraction and portal/biliary obstruction are key supporting features of mass-forming cholangiocarcinoma.
column9:
